title: Impact of Unexpected Dovish Fed Announcements on Bank Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Short‐horizon event study (difference-in-differences in time relative to the announcement).  

Why this fits:  
• The policy shock is date–specific and common to all listed banks.  
• Stock-market efficiency implies that any causal effect should be incorporated immediately in prices, so abnormal returns around day 0 isolate the impact.  

Key assumptions  
1. Exogeneity of the shock – the dovish surprise is orthogonal to firm-level fundamentals in the two-day window.  
2. No latent information leakage – no anticipation before the window and no other confounding macro news in the same window.  
3. Market model validity – beta estimated in the pre-event window captures the normal covariance between the stock and the market.  

Under these assumptions the mean cumulative abnormal return (CAR) in the event window is an unbiased estimate of the causal effect of the Fed’s dovish surprise on bank equity values.

## 2. R Code
```r
###############################################################################
# Impact of Unexpected Dovish Fed Announcements on Bank Stock Returns
# Full, self-contained R script
###############################################################################
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# 1. Read the data ------------------------------------------------------------
df <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s60_data.csv")

# sanity
print(head(df))

# 2. Define windows -----------------------------------------------------------
est_win  <- -30:-6      # estimation window for normal returns
event_win <- -1:1       # main CAR window
alt_win   <- -2:2       # robustness window

# 3. Compute Abnormal Returns -------------------------------------------------
# (Beta already supplied; we assume alpha = 0 market model)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(AR = ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# 4. Aggregate to CAR per stock ----------------------------------------------
car_main <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE))

car_alt <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% alt_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR_alt = sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE))

# merge
car <- left_join(car_main, car_alt, by = "stock_id")

# 5. Average treatment effect -------------------------------------------------
main_t <- t.test(car$CAR)
alt_t  <- t.test(car$CAR_alt)

cat("\n================  Event Study Results  ================\n")
cat("Mean CAR  (-1,+1):", round(main_t$estimate,4), 
    "  t-stat:", round(main_t$statistic,2), 
    "  p-value:", round(main_t$p.value,4), "\n")

cat("Mean CAR (-2,+2):", round(alt_t$estimate,4), 
    "  t-stat:", round(alt_t$statistic,2), 
    "  p-value:", round(alt_t$p.value,4), "\n")

# 6. Cross-sectional robustness: does CAR vary with beta? ---------------------
robust_reg <- lm(CAR ~ 1 + I(beta[match(stock_id, df$stock_id[df$event_day==0])]), 
                 data = car)
cat("\nCross-sectional regression of CAR on beta:\n")
print(tidy(robust_reg))

# 7. Placebo test (shift event by +10 days) -----------------------------------
placebo <- df %>% 
  mutate(event_day_shift = event_day - 10) %>% 
  filter(event_day_shift %in% event_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR_placebo = sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE))

placebo_t <- t.test(placebo$CAR_placebo)

cat("\nPlacebo Mean CAR (shifted +10 days):", round(placebo_t$estimate,4),
    "  t-stat:", round(placebo_t$statistic,2),
    "  p-value:", round(placebo_t$p.value,4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Because a dovish (interest-rate cutting) surprise should lower funding costs and increase net interest margins for banks in the short run, I expect a positive and statistically significant CAR. Typical magnitudes observed in prior literature are in the 1–2 % range over a (−1,+1) window. Therefore:  

• Sign: positive.  
• Magnitude: ≈ +1.2 % mean CAR, with a t-stat around 3–4, robust to alternative windows, and near‐zero in the placebo test.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare bank stock returns around the event day to assess the impact of the announcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Unexpected dovish Fed announcements lead to a decrease in bank stock CAR.
